title: dublin_node_street searches only a 3x3 cell window, not the documented 3-tile radius — false 'no street within 3 tiles' fallbacks
detail: Cells are 1 tile; the ±1-cell window covers at most ~1.5 tiles from the node. A street 2.0 tiles away (< 3.0) lives outside the window: never examined, so the fallback fires despite a street within the documented radius; 'nearest' is also only nearest-in-window.
recommended_fix: Expand the scan radius to ceil(DUBLIN_SEG_MAX_DIST) cells (a ±3 loop), or early-exit when a found segment's distance is below the window boundary, matching the documented 3-tile contract.

title: Node-without-street log line fires every frame per node, not 'one-shot' as commented and claimed
detail: dublin_node_block_draw is called from draw_building every frame per node (view.odin:1121-1126); there is no once-guard. A single fallback node spams stdout ~60 lines/sec, contradicting the 'one-shot log line' comment and PR claim.
recommended_fix: Deduplicate per node (e.g. a once-set keyed by node id, or log only on the first frame a node draws) so each node logs at most once per run.

title: Map_Board.render_dots + its parse loop are orphaned — the view no longer draws them and the core comment still claims it does
evidence:
// the 1-in-6 RENDER dots: the RAW sub-tile points (the blessed gallery's
	dotted-street texture — the dots sit at ~14 m spacing along streets, so
	they render as a dotted line, not individual buildings). The view draws
	these; the sim spawns from `candidates` (the snapped pool) — the two
	can never disagree (both derive from the same stride-6 subsample).
	render_dots: [dynamic][2]f32,
...
	// the render dots (raw sub-tile points — the gallery's dotted texture)
	b.render_dots = make([dynamic][2]f32, 0, len(snapped), allocator)
detail: This diff deleted the dot draw ('NO ... spawn-dot speckle' in dublin.odin's header). grep over app/, harness/, demos/ finds zero render_dots consumers; only core/map_test.odin:114 still pins the dead data. ~21k points parsed per board load for nothing; the contract comment is now false.
recommended_fix: Follow-up cleanup: drop the render_dots field, its load block, and its map_test assertion (or update the comments to state no consumer), keeping the change out of sim hashes.

title: Committed bake tool defaults to a personal absolute worktree path — which is not even this worktree
evidence:
exec(open("/Users/moses/.herdr/worktrees/packet-plumber/packet-plumber-v2-dublin-map-beautify/.scratch/blender_board_build.py").read())
...
WT = os.environ.get("PP_WT") or "/Users/moses/.herdr/worktrees/packet-plumber/packet-plumber-v2-dublin-map-beautify"  # the packet-plumber root (PP_WT overrides)
detail: The committed underlay-bake pipeline defaults to /Users/moses/... without the '-r1' suffix — on a fresh clone (or this machine, PP_WT unset) it silently reads/writes the wrong tree. The committed asset is not reproducible from the repo as committed.
recommended_fix: Derive WT from __file__ (../../.. of tools/blender_board/) like render_dublin_preview.py does, keeping PP_WT as an explicit override; fix the docstring exec path.

title: prep_board_geometry.py re-implements layout_clusters' pool/seed selection verbatim in main()
evidence:
# rebuild the cluster mapping (same math as layout_clusters' seeds)
    cands = asset["spawn_candidates"]
    pool = []
    for i in range(0, len(cands), 6):
        p = cands[i]
        pool.append((i, round(p[0]), round(p[1])))
detail: The pool build + 4x3 seed snap is copy-pasted from layout_clusters (lines 86-125). If one copy changes, lastmile/blobs silently diverge from terminals/routers in the bake. Line 15's sys.path.insert(0, "tools") is also dead (only shapely is imported).
recommended_fix: Extract the pool/seed computation into one helper both layout_clusters and main() call; drop the unused sys.path.insert.

title: dublin_shot.odin docstring still describes the removed candidate-dots + label look
detail: This diff removed the spawn-dot texture and district labels from the board ('NO district labels, NO tile grid, NO spawn-dot speckle'); the capture verb's header still promises candidates/labels in the frame.
recommended_fix: Update the docstring to the baked-underlay framing (underlay texture + attribution only).

title: dublin_node_street claims 'no libm' while importing core:math and calling math.sqrt
detail: The doc asserts 'no libm' but the file imports core:math (line 29) and calls math.sqrt. IEEE sqrt is exact/deterministic so behavior is fine; only the comment is inaccurate.
recommended_fix: Rephrase the comment (e.g. 'no transcendentals; sqrt is IEEE-exact') or hoist the direction normalization to avoid the claim mismatch.
